title: Energy R5B historical expectations-event case: Equinor Q4 2024

case.why: Issuer invitation stated consensus would be published one week before the 5 Feb result; independent 29 Jan article records company-collected values from 24 analysts; current issuer archive reproduces the same core values.
case.confounder: Q4 results were released with the 2025 Capital Markets Update, including strategy/capex/free-cash-flow/capital-distribution information, so event price movement cannot be attributed to earnings surprise alone.

sources.used_for: result date and issuer statement that consensus is published a week before actual release
pre-event company-collected consensus values and 24-analyst count
Q4 2024 collected January 2025 values, EPS, method and contributor count
sources.limitation: current archive compilation; exact historical byte/version publication timestamp not independently archived

sources.used_for: actual adjusted operating income, adjusted EPS, production, result context and simultaneous CMU
exact actual adjusted operating income after tax and adjusted net income distinction
Nasdaq-reported EQNR NO earnings-related implied move and actual earnings move
sources.limitation: external event-move context; not a Mastermind-reproduced return window

sources.used_for: data-quality conflict example; article maps USD1.733bn to after-tax adjusted operating result, while issuer statements distinguish USD2.292bn adjusted operating income after tax and USD1.733bn adjusted net income
sources.limitation: do not promote third-party mislabeled metric over issuer definitions

acceptance_cases: Require evidence the estimate existed before the result before labelling it pre-event consensus.
A current historical archive is not by itself an exact historical-byte publication receipt.
Independent pre-event reporting can strengthen first-known evidence without becoming the canonical metric owner.
Preserve contributor count and aggregation method with every consensus observation.
Compare only definition-matched consensus and actual metrics.
Do not map adjusted net income to adjusted operating income after tax.
Do not infer the sign of a stock move from one surprise metric when other matched metrics differ.
Do not attribute event return to earnings surprise when a capital-markets update is released concurrently.
Keep issuer-reported actuals above third-party relabeling when definitions conflict.
Issuer historical archive values may be used as archival context even when exact historical byte timestamp is unknown, but the evidence grade must say so.
An exchange-reported earnings move is contextual evidence, not a Mastermind-reproduced return series.
Do not transform implied move into expected direction; implied move is magnitude.
Keep event date, estimate publication date, archive retrieval date, result date and market-return window distinct.
Do not backfill later restatements or later classifications into the pre-event information set without explicit versioning.
A historical expectations-event case does not create ranking, entry, sizing, trade or predictive authority.
Historical surprise labels remain descriptive until repeated, predeclared out-of-sample evaluation establishes decision value.

next_case_requirements.goal: cleaner ordinary-quarter case without simultaneous capital-markets update
next_case_requirements.candidate: Equinor Q1 or Q2 2025, or Fortum Q2 2026 where first-known evidence can be proven
